title: Network Topologies: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Networks are laid out like city streets. Bus, star, ring and mesh are the main shapes. And each one has a catch.

scenes.heading: City streets
scenes.narration: Think of how the roads are arranged. A bus is one main road, with a driveway to each house. A star puts every house on its own road to a central square. A ring is a circular road, where traffic goes round one way. A mesh has roads from every house to every other house.

scenes.heading: Strengths and weaknesses
scenes.narration: Here is the trade-off. A star is cheap, but a mesh needs many links and ports. In a star, one cable failure loses one device, but a mesh just reroutes. The star's weak point is the central device.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. A star can use a hub or a switch. A basic ring sends data in one direction. And mesh is the most expensive.

items.wrong: A star always uses a hub

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Star is the most common, and mesh is the most resilient. Physical is the cabling, and logical is how data flows. A bus shares one collision domain. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva topologies lab.
